title: Australia's influence declining in the region - ABC Pacific
text:
Australia's influence declining in the region - ABC Pacific

Program: Australia's influence declining in the region

Program: Pacific Beat

Wed 19 Jul 2017 at 3:00pm Wed 19 Jul 2017 at 3:00pm Wed 19 Jul 2017 at 3:00pm

The author of a new book on Australian policy in the Pacific says while Australia might consider itself to be the natural regional leader, an inconsistent strategy of engagement with its neighbours has seen its influence decline in recent years.

Joanne Wallis from the Strategic and Defence Studies Centre interviewed former Australian Prime Ministers, foreign ministers, diplomats and defence officials for her book Pacific Power? Australia's strategy in the Pacific Islands.

Wallis says while many politicians and officials agree on the South Pacific's geographic and strategic importance to Australia, the region has never been a priority for foreign and defence policy.
